title: Global prime-power quotient isomorphisms induce the canonical local quotient system
statement: Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $\mathfrak p\subset C$ and $Q\subset D$ be prime ideals with $f^{-1}(Q)=\mathfrak p$, and write $KD$ for the ideal generated by $f(K)$ for an ideal $K\subseteq C$. Suppose that for every integer $n\geq1$ the canonical map $\alpha_n:C/\mathfrak p^n\to D/\mathfrak p^nD$, $[c]\mapsto[f(c)]$, is an isomorphism. Then $Q=\mathfrak pD$ and $Q^n=\mathfrak p^nD$ for all $n\geq1$. The canonical local homomorphism $f_{\rm loc}:C_{\mathfrak p}\to D_Q$, $c/s\mapsto f(c)/f(s)$, has inverse image of $QD_Q$ equal to $\mathfrak pC_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For each $n\geq1$ its induced map $e_n:C_{\mathfrak p}/(\mathfrak pC_{\mathfrak p})^n\to D_Q/(QD_Q)^n$ is a ring isomorphism, with $e_n([c/s])=[f(c)/f(s)]$. For all $k\geq n\geq1$, these maps commute with the quotient transition maps from exponent $k$ to exponent $n$.

proof.text: First $\mathfrak pD\subseteq Q$, since $f(\mathfrak p)\subseteq Q$. For $d\in Q$, surjectivity of $\alpha_1$ gives $c\in C$ with $d-f(c)\in\mathfrak pD\subseteq Q$. Thus $f(c)\in Q$, whence $c\in f^{-1}(Q)=\mathfrak p$ and $d\in\mathfrak pD$. Therefore $Q=\mathfrak pD$. This uses only the exponent-one hypothesis and does not assume that $\mathfrak p$ is maximal.

proof.text: Apply extension of ideal powers to $f$: $Q^n=(\mathfrak pD)^n=\mathfrak p^nD$ for every $n\geq1$. Apply the same statement to $C\to C_{\mathfrak p}$ and $D\to D_Q$: writing $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pC_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak n=QD_Q$, we have $\mathfrak m^n=\mathfrak p^nC_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak n^n=Q^nD_Q$.

proof.text: The canonical localRingHom is a local homomorphism. The extended primes are the maximal ideals of the two prime localizations, and a local homomorphism contracts the target maximal ideal to the source maximal ideal. Thus its contraction is exactly the extended prime. Mapping ideals commutes with powers, so this map induces canonical quotient maps at every exponent. Mathlib localRingHom_mk' gives their fraction formula.

proof.text: Apply the quotient-localization instance of Tag 00CT to both rings: the local rings modulo the extensions of I and J are localizations of C/I and D/J at the images of the respective prime complements. Here I is p^n, J is I.map f = Q^n, and extension commutes with powers by Step 2.

source.place: Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), its explicit fraction maps and inverse; elementary application to the given quotient isomorphisms

proof.text: Let e be the given quotient isomorphism C/I to D/J. Its image of the denominator submonoid is exactly the target denominator submonoid. The forward inclusion follows from p = Q.comap f. For the reverse inclusion, lift the class of any d outside Q to the class of c in C/I. Since J is contained in Q, equality of the classes of f(c) and d implies that f(c) is outside Q; hence c is outside p. Mathlib ringEquivOfRingEquiv now induces an isomorphism of the two localized quotients. It is the canonical quotient map of the localRingHom: apply quotient ring-homomorphism extensionality and localization ring-homomorphism extensionality; on the image of c both maps give the class of f(c)/1. This proves bijectivity of each canonical local quotient map.

source.place: Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), its explicit fraction maps and inverse; elementary application to the given quotient isomorphisms

proof.text: For k greater than or equal to n, powers decrease and the quotient transition maps exist. Define e_n as RingEquiv.ofBijective of the canonical local quotient map. The fraction formula follows from quotientMap_mk and localRingHom_mk'. For transition compatibility choose a representative x in C_p of a class modulo the kth power. Both composites are definitionally the class of localRingHom(x) modulo the nth power, so quotient surjectivity proves the equality.

lean.statement: theorem adic_quotient_isomorphisms_localize {C : Type u} {D : Type v} [CommRing C] [CommRing D] (f : C →+* D) (p : Ideal C) (Q : Ideal D) [p.IsPrime] [Q.IsPrime] (hpQ : p = Q.comap f) (hquot : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap ((p ^ n).map f) f (Ideal.le_comap_map : p ^ n ≤ ((p ^ n).map f).comap f))) : Q = p.map f ∧ (∀ n : ℕ+, Q ^ (n : ℕ) = (p ^ (n : ℕ)).map f) ∧ (Q.map (algebraMap D (Localization.AtPrime Q))).comap (Localization.localRingHom p Q f hpQ) = p.map (algebraMap C (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∧ ∃ e : ∀ n : ℕ+, (Localization.AtPrime p ⧸ (p.map (algebraMap C (Localization.AtPrime p))) ^ (n : ℕ)) ≃+* (Localization.AtPrime Q ⧸ (Q.map (algebraMap D (Localization.AtPrime Q))) ^ (n : ℕ)), (∀ (n : ℕ+) (c : C) (s : p.primeCompl), e n (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (IsLocalization.mk' (Localization.AtPrime p) c s)) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (IsLocalization.mk' (Localization.AtPrime Q) (f c) (⟨f s, le_comap_primeCompl_iff.mpr (ge_of_eq hpQ) s.2⟩ : Q.primeCompl))) ∧ (∀ (k n : ℕ+) (hnk : n ≤ k) (x : Localization.AtPrime p ⧸ (p.map (algebraMap C (Localization.AtPrime p))) ^ (k : ℕ)), e n (Ideal.Quotient.factor (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right hnk) x) = Ideal.Quotient.factor (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right hnk) (e k x))
